files.coverage_caveat: See PORT_STATUS.md for modes, invariants, intentional differences and missing operations.
Core signature, phase/permutation, interning, decomposition, statistics and lifecycle are reviewed and validated; fixed-name output and exact print side effects are replaced by owned data.

The complete checking translation unit is represented by AigManager.Check. It strictly covers C terminal fanin rules, internal two-fanin/canonical ordering, structural-hash identity and entry counts, and live object accounting, while additionally validating topological fanins, CI/CO order, levels, exact phases, reference counts, register/constraint partitions, tombstones and choice-chain shape/cycles. Errors replace stdout diagnostics and assertions. Aig_ManCheckPhase is enforced on every Check call rather than exposed separately. Aig_ManCheckMarkA needs no runtime API because AigObject has no persistent traversal marks; algorithms own local mark slices, so the asserted condition is structurally guaranteed. Corruption tests target constant/terminal/hash/fanin/level/phase/reference invariants, and Go-only AIG operation fuzzing checks the manager after every mutation, cleanup and clone.
Complete reviewed AIG cut enumeration, truth composition, dominance, cost, implication and factoring behavior is implemented with owned snapshots and independent exhaustive/fuzz validation.

All functions in this source have concrete Go paths or owned-state replacements. Iterative signed structural-supergate collection preserves fanin-zero-first order, same-polarity deduplication, opposite-polarity contradiction collapse, complemented/type/dynamic-reference boundaries and source scratch ownership for the CNF AIG mapping scan. Core iterative DFS covers CO-rooted node-only/full preorder and postorder, all-object and explicit-root variants, ordered CI support, DAG size, cut-internal postorder, maximum output level, level buckets and a topology check strengthened by manager validation. The fixed-16 support diagnostic is a non-printing shared-budget count, matching all 32 native counts and independently tested beyond the threshold. All ordered fields, including cut volumes, match 24 native graphs; buffers, dangling/missing-boundary errors, ownership, limits/cancellation and 10,000-node cones are checked. Reverse fanout DFS builds owned object-order fanout lists and returns every AND/buffer in fanout-first postorder, including dangling logic; all 32 native orders match and buffer/deep/fuzz invariants are checked. Cone mark/count/clean/unmark scratch helpers are represented by an owned Boolean mask with identical AND-cone membership and count; all 32 native mark arrays match and Go has no generic object data to clear. Concrete optional choice-successor storage participates in append, clone, cleanup and manager validation. Ordinary DFS preserves native equivalence ordering, dedicated choice DFS preserves fanin-zero/fanin-one/successor postorder, and owned choice levels avoid mutating structural levels. Timing-box topology and level dependencies validate exact terminal ownership and reject cycles rather than accepting traversal-mark artifacts. All traversal arrays and no-box levels match 32 native cases; all box levels and topology answers match another 32 native cases, including invalid object order. Atomic chain configuration, malformed timing associations, cycles, limits/cancellation, 10,001 alternatives, 10,000 boxes and semantic equivalence are checked. Cone transfer and CI composition preserve native indexed-CI mapping, complement phases and structural hashing while using iterative traversal and atomic clone commits. Exact returned literals and complete object layouts match 32 native cases; constant/same-manager behavior, arbitrary internal replacement functions, semantic projection, limits/cancellation and a 10,000-node cone are checked.

Partial concrete SatSolver3 facade over the validated owned CDCL engine. Construction/default and explicit seeds, variable growth, atomic original-clause loading, root simplification, pushed-assumption propagation/pop, composed solve/internal solve, relative/absolute conflict and propagation limits, restart, model/final-conflict/count/statistics access, checked activity and polarity controls, runtime/random controls, owned bookmark/rollback, memory/lifecycle, lexical SAT and deterministic order-preserving assumption minimization are implemented. Lexical search is exhaustively checked across every three-variable truth subset and a fresh 5,000-case arbitrary-CNF fuzzer. Remaining source work includes the specialized unit-learning minimizer, explicit learned-clause insertion compatibility, direct reduce/propagate entry dispositions, pivot/frequency experiments and solver3-specific trace/store attachment or reuse dispositions.

Partial public-header facade and complete ordered gate-builder family. Model literals/final conflicts, compression through checked simplification, polarity controls, runtime/random controls, bookmark/rollback and Go lifetime are represented. Constant, buffer, enabled-buffer, complemented-output AND, XOR, mux, four-to-one mux, XOR-AND, constraint and half-sorter clauses preserve source order and load atomically; exhaustive Go truth models cover their intended semantics and the mux source quirk is pinned. Remaining declarations are the specialized second minimizer, pivot/frequency experiment state, and explicit solver3 trace/proof-store/util compatibility wiring or dispositions.

Owned concrete fanout snapshots replace the manager-attached intrusive circular lists. Build order, fanout pins, removal order and tail reinsertion match 32 native cases. Native FanoutStart's no-buffer precondition is enforced; buffer-aware read-only traversal remains available separately. Limits, cancellation, 10,000 fanouts and independent fuzz reconstruction of every structural/reference edge are checked.

All 48 native combinations of one through three frames and initialization/output/register/enlargement flags match complete CI/CO partitions, object arenas and cleanup-filtered source-object-major maps. Native unchecked zero-frame and buffer cases return typed errors; explicit object/mapping limits and cancellation bound construction. All 32 permanent native cases match and semantic fuzzing compares size and ordered support with an independent recursive transaction.

All thirteen active definitions have concrete Go paths. Construction, connection/disconnection, iterative recursive deletion, CO deletion/patching and owned formatting retain stable-ID-safe behavior. Object replacement and buffer-fanin repair/propagation use an independently owned atomic rebuild: every old use is substituted, all buffer chains are bypassed, CI/CO and sequential partitions are retained, and an explicit old-to-new literal map replaces native transient forward-pointing buffers that violate AigManager's topological invariant. Thirty-two retained mutation cases match complete native arenas where IDs remain stable; exhaustive Boolean tests cover forward-ID replacement and buffer chains, a 10,000-node case proves iterative depth safety, and standalone replacement fuzzing passed 2,419,984 executions. Go removes deleted COs from its authoritative output slice and returns owned graphs/strings instead of retaining stale entries or writing stdout.

Forward-frontier retiming is implemented as an owned, atomic transform with iterative reachability marking and dependency-driven normalization. All three source functions have concrete Go behavior. Thirty-two phase/step cases match a narrowly corrected native oracle in every CI, CO, register count and object field; transition-language tests independently compare all one-step behaviors after one warmup frame, which excludes invalid arbitrary encodings of newly introduced state. The pinned native entry point is not itself a usable oracle: Aig_ManSetRegNum stores CIO IDs in the pNext union field that its marking assertions require to be null, and after a real retiming step Aig_ManDupOrdered dereferences a future CI before copying it. The recorded oracle avoids the first unrelated setup conflict and replaces only final duplication with CI precreation plus DFS cone copying. Tests also cover source ownership, malformed and combinational inputs, exact object limits, cancellation and 10,000 levels; semantic fuzzing passes. Go normalizes a zero MaxSteps option to a one-million safety limit rather than preserving native's accidental do-while single step for zero.

Owned atomic CI remapping plus sequential cleanup cover Aig_ManRemap and both native cleanup modes. Thirty-two substitution cases match native CI/CO order, register/constraint counts and every object field after signed CI, constant and cross-register replacement; semantic fuzzing exhaustively compares all assignments. Remapping precreates every terminal, collapses buffers, structurally rebuilds ANDs and preserves source ownership, while rejecting choice metadata rather than silently dropping it. Another 32 register-dependency cases match native full and slot-preserving cleanup arenas. Native full cleanup leaves redundant allocation/deletion counters stale and fails its own Aig_ManCheck, while Go matches observable structure and requires stronger validation. Tests cover malformed inputs, exact limits, cancellation and 10,000 levels. Duplicate-latch counting/reduction, SCC computation, partitioned sweeping and the high-level sequential-cleanup pipeline remain unported.

Deterministic owned DOT generation and explicit file output cover both source functions. Sixteen exhaustive phase/style cases match native output byte-for-byte, including ranks, object order, constant visibility, dangling nodes, complement edge styles and bold nodes. HAIG is accepted but has no active effect, matching the source whose HAIG-specific blocks are commented out. Graph marks and temporary CO levels become local slices/calculation, so rendering never mutates the manager. The native 200-AND default is preserved, with additional object, byte and cancellation limits; errors are returned instead of printed. WriteShowDOT preserves final-extension replacement and returns the written path but deliberately does not launch Abc_ShowFile or any external viewer. Tests cover file failures, invalid bold IDs, ownership and 10,000 nodes; deterministic structural fuzzing passes.

Graph core only. See PORT_STATUS.md for missing GIA algorithms/modes, raw duplicate handling, source scratch preservation and native XOR/mux lowering. Fixed-primary-input cofactors use iterative reachable-cone copying, preserve CI/CO/register/constraint layout and extend native node semantics without source scratch mutation. Single-output combinational cofactor mux composition shares CI order and checked gate copying; constraints must agree and are preserved. Guarded combinational object cofactors preserve metadata and safely handle COs ordered before the pivot, unlike the C single-pass unset-guard case. Combinational output-index/mask selection retains all CIs, raw DFS-ordered gate kinds and selected output order. Constraint suffix semantics are preserved/validated. Sequential PO cone extraction preserves dynamic register discovery order and optional original-order PI trimming, exposing source terminal-index maps and retaining validated constraint suffixes. Combinational gate/CI/constant root extraction optionally trims PIs and exposes source PI indices. Sequential inputs are rejected because this C variant disables register construction. Absolute-forward-level and first-visit depth cone cuts expose source boundary IDs, preserve memoization/root-order behavior and handle extended node edges explicitly. Exactly-one generation emits violation outputs (all false iff exactly one selected input is true), not positive assumptions; zero variables are rejected. Levelized duplication retains dangling gates and explicit source-object maps; extends the ordinary-AND C path to raw buffers/XORs/muxes and preserves constraint metadata. Stable ID order handles same-level buffer dependencies. Explicit-list duplication validates unique typed IDs and dependency order, returns owned maps, and assigns caller-specified register suffixes. Constraint roles are not inherited, matching this C API; raw extended node kinds are preserved. Structural sorted CI support sets include buffers, CO drivers and native mux controls, with bounded total entries and owned output copies. These are structural rather than minimized functional supports. Conjunctive constraint extraction uses iterative unique DFS boundaries and highest-level first-tie selection. Its constraint output deliberately complements C violation polarity to provide a positive assumption. Extended nodes remain opaque boundaries; invalid roots/pre-existing constraints are rejected. Output support ranking preserves minimum maximum one, first largest index and exact nonstable two-way quicksort/selection-sort tie order; the C QuickSort3 entry point delegates to QuickSort2. Support-normalized reduction returns source-output support projections and reduced-output indices, with optional first-occurrence phased-literal deduplication. It copies actual single-support logic rather than C shortcut, supports extended nodes, and rejects sequential/constraint graphs requiring caller policy. This is per-cone input renaming, not whole-network equivalence. Gate-output duplication preserves all dangling/raw extended gates and source CO mappings. New regular-value gate POs precede the preserved constraint suffix and RIs; C drops constraint roles. Support-limited slicing retains all within-limit gates and exposes those feeding omitted gates or source COs. Native mux control support/boundaries are included; returned regular source root IDs describe the combinational slice collection, with no register/constraint roles. One-hot attachment constrains PIs combinationally or register outputs sequentially, adapting native violation polarity and moving new assumptions before RIs. Existing constraints/raw extended nodes are preserved; zero selected variables are rejected. Shared-PI composition retains separate first/second register banks and owned maps for both sources, hashes extended node semantics, and preserves grouped constraint suffixes rather than dropping roles as C does. Induction miter computes I(state) AND NOT I(nextState), ignoring transition properties/constraints like C; this is not a complete safety certificate. Explicit invariant constant mapping and extended gate lowering avoid source scratch dependence. Property-cone attachment supports all-CI and RO-only mappings, constant/repeated cones, summed mapping caps and explicit constraint-suffix preservation; constrained/sequential/misdimensioned cone inputs are rejected. Shared register hold control is a new first PI: true updates, false holds. Original PO/constraint functions and register order survive; reset lists remain caller-owned. Flop-class extraction accepts explicit class labels, externalizes other registers, and returns CI/CO/reset projection indices. Raw gates and constraint suffixes survive; this is a state abstraction requiring caller interpretation. Single-output existential and first-output universal PI quantification retain all CIs. Universal later outputs are positive cofactors, matching C. Sequential/constraint graphs are rejected; extended nodes are copied semantically. All-output existential quantification uses reachable DFS copying and preserves register/constraint roles. It quantifies each CO independently, not the joint transition relation; per-coordinate witnesses may disagree. Register-phase recoding preserves raw gate kinds, dangling logic, terminal order and constraint roles; known resets must be XOR-transformed by callers, unknown resets remain unknown. PI/register permutations validate bijections and use new-to-old direction, preserving raw gates and constraints. Register permutations pair ROs/RIs; callers reorder resets identically. Register spreading inserts zero-next-state dummy slots and preserves raw gates/constraints. Spread consumes source registers in order for any non--1 entry; gap permutation instead validates explicit source indices. Reset projection/dummy resets are caller-owned. Trailing-PI retention raw-copies all logic and rejects any omitted-input dependency, including dangling logic, rather than using unset C scratch. It is combinational only and preserves constraint roles. Independent replication shares only constant zero, groups copy-major PI/RO and ordinary/constraint/RI banks, and preserves raw gates. Go normalizes physical terminal placement instead of using C reordered terminal tables; reset lists repeat copy-major. Register abstraction externalizes explicitly ordered registers as pseudo-PIs, drops their RIs, copies only retained output cones and returns CI/CO/reset projections. Constraints and extended nodes survive; invalid abstraction mappings are rejected. Serial combinational composition connects bottom COs to top CIs, preserves top constraints and lowers extended gates. Bottom constraints are rejected pending explicit caller data/assumption policy. State-property replacement maps property inputs to transition ROs and retains original RIs. Both property and transition constraint sets are preserved, extending C which drops original POs/constraint roles. Ordered CI remapping validates constants and same/earlier CI references, supports self-phase and composed aliases, and checks selected signal outputs/RI dimensions. Nil outputs preserve roles; custom outputs explicitly define trailing RIs and have no constraints. Raw paired-output duplication doubles every CO including RIs and retains original register count, exactly matching C. It changes transition layout and intentionally drops constraint roles; no state-equivalence claim is made. Interleaved block extraction keeps every stride-th CI/CO, zeros other CIs, floors register count by stride and drops constraints exactly as C. Terminal divisibility and resource/cancellation limits are checked. Direct-PI/constant PO trimming discounts PO references before trimming PIs, retains all ROs/RIs/raw gates and returns terminal projections with -1 dummies. Constraint roles are cleared like C; dangling source gates are safely retained rather than asserting. Adjacent/split-half paired-output XOR miters preserve RIs and clear constraint roles like C. The history-swept pair selector excludes both constant-zero and constant-one comparisons, matching the source despite its NonZero name; it is not an equivalence verdict. Source signal-name metadata remains unported. General trimming supports unused PIs, selected constant phases, dual-pair selection/sweeping and dummy terminals with explicit composed CI/CO/register projections. Dual trimming requires zero initialization and excludes both constant XOR phases like C. Constraint roles are cleared; source signal-name metadata remains unported. Dual-output conversion pairs each PO with zero without cleanup, while half interleaving reorders POs and performs cleanup. Both preserve RIs and clear source constraint roles exactly as C. Dual-side DFS traversal includes extended control edges. Smaller-side-first hashing swaps adjacent PO pairs only when even-side node count is larger; ties retain order, shared cones are hashed once, and source constraint roles are cleared. Zero/one/unknown reset normalization implements default raw mode with added initial-value PIs and a zero-to-one selector register, retaining extra unused PI slots. It preserves constraints/raw extended nodes and includes native mux-control-only fanouts; fGiaSimple degenerate-AND mode and signal-name metadata remain unported. Dispositioned declaration-only compatibility header. It contains no inline logic or data definitions, is selected by no module.make or top-level build manifest, has no callers in this snapshot, and every declared solver_new/solver_addClause/solver_solve/value/model/conflict symbol lacks a definition across src. Creating a Go implementation would invent semantics rather than port source behavior; native Go SAT functionality is provided by the independently validated concrete bsat and msat ports.

The build manifest is fully reconciled: each of its 13 selected translation units is independently validated in this ledger. The Go package uses concrete owned vectors, clauses, arenas, order heap, queue and solver state rather than reproducing C compilation or linkage. The build-disabled msatOrderJ.c alternative is also validated separately but correctly remains outside this manifest's selected list.

The complete linked external MSAT surface is represented by concrete MsatSolver, MsatIntVector, MsatClauseVector, MsatVariableOrder, MsatStatus, SatVar and SatLit operations. Typed status and literal operations replace macros; copied slices replace exposed arrays; owned diagnostics replace FILE/stdout procedures. Six solver declarations (ReadTruth, SetProofWriting, SetVarTypeA, SetVarMap, ReadSolutions and ReadSolutionsArray) and the entire Msat_VarHeap declaration family have no definition anywhere in this source snapshot and are explicitly dispositioned as stale declaration-only API rather than invented behavior. Their implemented ordering successor is msatOrderH.c.

Complete concrete MSAT variable/clause activity state integrated with MsatVariableOrder and MsatClauseVector. Negative variable decay disables bumps, float64 increment/decay rules, heap updates, 1e100 variable rescaling, float32 clause rounding and 1e20 learned-clause rescaling are preserved. Checked finite arithmetic, atomic learned-database validation, copied snapshots and detachable lifecycle replace unchecked shared solver fields.

All 21 active definitions are represented by the concrete MsatClauseContext and MsatClause operations: original and learned creation, top-level simplification/enqueue, stable identity and fields, activity, locking, watched propagation, simplification, reason calculation, watch removal, destruction and deterministic formatting. Original clauses intentionally correct the source's documented duplicate/opposite-polarity bug: equal literals collapse and opposite polarities satisfy the clause. Copied input/literal views, checked limits and invariants, finite activity writes, atomic activity rollback and idempotent lifecycle replace raw aliases, assertions and manual allocation. Go-only unit tests and independent normalization/truth and watched-propagation fuzz models cover the implementation.

Complete bounded owned MSAT clause-reference vector. Native small-capacity rounding, exact Grow, doubling Push, shrink/clear, pop and indexed replacement/read behavior are preserved. Copied pointer-array snapshots prevent structural aliasing while retaining stable clause identity; checked errors and idempotent Close replace assertions and manual free.

The internal header is fully reconciled to concrete Go ownership. MsatSolver and MsatSolverStats cover every stored solver field through checked state or copied accessors; MsatClause, MsatClauseVector, MsatIntVector, MsatQueue, MsatVariableOrder and the three arena types cover all internal forward declarations and layouts. Typed values replace unassigned/order sentinels and printing macros. Every declaration with a linked definition is covered by its validated translation unit. ClauseCreateFake, ClauseCreateFakeLit and ClauseComputeTruth are declaration-only in this snapshot with no definition or caller and are explicitly not invented.

All 15 active definitions are represented by concrete owned fixed, flexible and step arenas. The fixed manager preserves the 1,024-entry/64-KiB chunk rule, minimum eight-entry chunks, LIFO recycling, peak/accounting, first-chunk restart and diagnostics. The flexible manager preserves MSAT's 4-KiB initial chunks, monotonic packing and two-times-large-request growth. The step manager preserves 8-byte power-of-two classes, exact size routing, immediate oversized allocation/release and class-only memory usage. Checked limits, stable handles, stale-handle invalidation and idempotent Close replace unchecked raw pointers and manual free.

Complete concrete MSAT activity max-heap selected by module.make. Native one-based heap/index storage, strict-greater ties, verbatim Clean layout, destructive selection with lazy assigned removal, reinsertion on unassign, upward activity updates, percolation and invariant checks are preserved. Owned assignment/activity arrays prepare direct integration with msatActivity.c; limits, atomic validation, copied snapshots and idempotent Close replace assertions and borrowed solver arrays.

Complete concrete port of the build-disabled J-boundary ordering alternative. MsatJBoundaryOrder owns cone membership, assignments, activities, adjacency and the circular insertion-ordered boundary. Assignment and unassignment update exactly the affected neighborhood; selection preserves strict-greater activity and stable ring-order ties. Checked bounds, cone isolation, copied snapshots, structural/semantic invariants and idempotent lifecycle replace shared solver pointers, assertions and diagnostic stdout. Unit tests cover transition order, ties, resizing, ownership and errors; an independent Go state-machine model passed 5,000 fuzz executions.

Complete owned fixed-capacity MSAT propagation queue. First/last cursor semantics preserve the source rule that extracted slots are unavailable until Clear; typed empty extraction replaces the ambiguous -1 sentinel. Checked limits, copied pending snapshots and idempotent Close replace assertions and manual allocation/free.

Complete bounded MSAT DIMACS loading is folded over the already validated strict CNF tokenizer/parser, then constructs and root-simplifies a concrete MsatSolver. Byte, line, variable, clause, literal and cancellation limits replace seek/ftell assumptions, unchecked integer overflow, process exit and partial solver leaks. Plain-file reads are bounded before allocation.

All 34 active definitions are represented by concrete MsatSolver lifecycle and copied state access. This includes allocation/resize/clean/close/Prepare, variable/clause/capacity/decision/reason/assignment/model/learned/watch/memory/seen access, checked allocation counters, clause lookup and Type-A/start marking, factors, adjacency/cone/used-variable state, verbosity and truth tables. Prepare installs an owned decision cone; the concrete enqueue mask preserves source variables-used filtering for assumptions and implications. Checked errors, copied nested snapshots, overflow-safe seen epochs and idempotent close replace assertions, mutable raw arrays and manual allocation.

All five active definitions are represented on concrete MsatSolver backed by the validated owned CDCL engine: variable growth, checked clause addition, progress estimation, deterministic statistics text and assumption solving with conflict/time budgets. Solver results retain MSAT -1/0/1 status values and copied literal-encoded models/conflicts. The Go budget is an exact safe limit rather than the C restart-loop overshoot, and zero-variable progress is defined as zero rather than NaN.

All four definitions are represented by owned deterministic diagnostics and DIMACS serialization/file output. Assignment, original/learned clause and activity formatting preserve native layout; callers may inject a timestamp for reproducibility. DIMACS includes live original/learned clauses and level-zero assertions, and intentionally emits an empty clause for an inconsistent solver so serialization cannot silently change UNSAT to SAT. Formatting completes before file creation.

All 13 active search definitions are represented by the concrete shared CDCL state machine and checked MsatSolver search operations. Assumption levels, enqueue filtering, watched propagation, one-level/all-level cancellation, first-UIP analysis, learned recording, root simplification, learned reduction/removal, recently-added original removal and bounded search are covered. Stable integer clause IDs replace raw pointers; copied conflicts, learned clauses, trails, reasons and watches prevent structural aliasing. Database rebuilds preserve all live original clauses including units while removing learned or marked storage atomically.

Complete deterministic learned-clause activity sorting. The fixed MiniSat pseudo-random pivot recurrence, selection cutoff at 15, recursive partitioning, float32 comparisons and equal/NaN behavior are preserved directly on stable clause pointers and MsatClauseVector storage. Invalid clauses reject atomically before mutation.

Complete bounded owned MSAT integer vector. Native small-capacity rounding, exact Grow, doubling Push, fill/shrink/clear, unique and ordered-unique insertion, signed sorting, pop and clone behavior are preserved. Explicit Take, Transfer and Release replace borrowed/moved raw-array aliases; copied Values replace mutable ReadArray, and checked errors replace assertions.
